text:
Alex: quick async check-in for SDKs / quickstarts / sample apps
What I did: merged python quickstart (PR #782), updated node quickstart to streaming API, and fixed a couple of README typos.
Blockers: sample-app `image-annotator` failing on Windows CI with path join errors. Also saw one dead docs link flagged by the checker.
Today: triage the sample CI, open a docs PR for the dead link, and get a Windows-aware reviewer on the sample fix.

Maya: I can take the windows CI failure. Which test is failing? send the CI link pls. :eyes:

Alex: here's the failing job: https://ci.internal/redwood/sdks/12345
Stack trace snippet:```
E   File "/workspace/sample-app/tests/test_runner.py", line 42, in test_load_assets
    p = os.path.join(base_dir, "assets")
E   AssertionError: expected file not found
```
Looks like join + backslash mismatch when telemetry loads fixtures.

Maya: ah yeah, classic. I can try swapping to pathlib for those tests. Quick fix: replace `os.path.join(base, 'assets')` with `Path(base) / 'assets'`. I'll open a PR and tag @Alex.

Alex: perfect, thx. PR link when ready.

TJ: FYI I hit a packaging wobble on mac M1 when building the native extension for the python SDK — wheels failing in `cargo build` step. Workaround I used locally: `export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0` before `pip wheel`. Pushed a branch `m1-wheel-fix`. CI is queued.

Sabrina: small docs nit: quickstart code shows `from redwood import RedwoodClient` but package name is now `redwood_inference` in py27/py310 builds. I'll open a docs PR to align examples. Also fixing a fenced code block that lost language hint.

Alex: thanks @Sabrina. Also the link-checker (docs-bot) flagged `/docs/old-quickstart` as 404 — easy replace to `/docs/quickstart/python`.

docs-bot: CI: PR #782 (python quickstart) -> ✅ checks passed. Link-checker: 1 broken link found in `site/content/quickstarts/index.md` -> `/docs/old-quickstart`.

Maya: opened sample-app PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/56 — uses pathlib, adds a tiny fixture loader test. cc @Alex for review.

Alex: reviewing now. Quick comment: can you add a Windows-specific CI job matrix row? if not, at least add the path test to the unit matrix so we catch regressions.

Maya: yea I'll add a windows job (runs on self-hosted workers) — will follow up in PR.

TJ: pushed `m1-wheel-fix` -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/789 CI started. If it flakes, might need infra to update mac runner toolchain.

Sabrina: docs PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 — fixes package import, adds language hints to code fences, and replaces the broken link with `/docs/quickstart/python`.

Alex: sweet. Plan for today: Maya to land sample-app pathlib fix + windows job, TJ to monitor wheel CI and loop in infra if it fails, Sabrina to land docs PR. I'll merge python quickstart follow-ups after CI. Ping me for reviews.

Maya: will try to land by EOD PT.

TJ: I'll keep an eye and ping infra if CI fails twice.

Sabrina: aiming to merge docs PR in next hour.

Alex: thanks all :rocket: any other small asks?

Maya: nudge — can somebody review the node streaming quickstart? PR link in #node-quickstarts channel, needs a quick sanity check on the example payload.

Alex: noted, I'll take a look after sample-app review.

TJ: +1 on quick review, I can also sanity-check the example payload.

Alex: great — that'll wrap it up for me. cheers all.
